answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must call MSHA at 1-800-746-1553 once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows or should know of an accident.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is a covered accident.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. Methane raises this figure by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane. Moisture in the mixture counts toward the incombustible content.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: Where methane is present in a ventilating current, the required percentage increases by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

claims.text: Moisture in the combined dust counts as part of the incombustible content.
claims.quote: Moisture contained in the combined coal dust, rock dust and other dusts shall be considered as a part of the incombustible content of such mixture.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Operators must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift, at a time other than a shift change, and must involve all persons underground.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. The training should be conducted in conditions that closely duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training should be conducted in conditions that closely duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA. That is equivalent to a dose of 100% of what the standard permits, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 (surface metal and nonmetal mines) and 57.9300 (underground metal and nonmetal mines). Both sections also require them where a drop-off is steep or deep enough to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.

claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be provided and maintained on the banks of roadways where a drop-off exists of sufficient grade or depth to cause a vehicle to overturn or endanger persons in equipment.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. (Under 30 CFR 75.1507, a refuge alternative may sustain persons for only 48 hours if advance arrangements are made for additional supplies.)
